subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@finsecure.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0000
Subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation follow-up

Hi Alex 

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and a couple of follow-ups so we can align on the right deployment path for FinSecure.

Recap:
- You're evaluating LLM-powered document summarization for internal compliance and customer support workflows.
- Primary constraint: regulated PII and transaction-level data cannot leave your VPC or be logged to a third-party service.
- Preferred outcomes: predictable latency (sub-300ms p50 for small requests), strict data isolation, KMS integration for key ownership.

Clarifying questions we need to resolve to recommend Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem):
1) When you say 'data cannot leave our VPC,' do you mean inference must run inside your VPC (no egress), or is it acceptable for data to traverse to a Redwood-managed Dedicated cluster if we can guarantee no persistent storage and customer KMS?
2) Do you require customer-managed KMS/HSM for model keying and log encryption, or is BYOK acceptable with Redwood-managed HSM?
3) Are there any audit log retention/forwarding requirements (SIEM ingestion) that would force logs to remain on your network?

Suggested next steps:
- If inference must run fully inside your VPC, Private VPC or on-prem package is likely required; we'll schedule a technical scoping call to map network flows.
- If a Dedicated (customer-dedicated GPU pool) endpoint is acceptable provided we disable telemetry and integrate with your KMS, we can produce an architecture and SLA.

I've attached a one-page mutual action plan template and our Private VPC architecture diagram to help guide the discussion. Can we schedule a 60-min technical call Thursday or Friday this week? Vivek (cc'd) is our solutions engineer who can run the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0172

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@finsecure.com>

Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation follow-up

Hi Marissa 

Thanks for the clear recap. A few answers inline below.

> 1) When you say 'data cannot leave our VPC,' do you mean inference must run inside your VPC (no egress), or is it acceptable for data to traverse to a Redwood-managed Dedicated cluster if we can guarantee no persistent storage and customer KMS?

We need inference to execute inside our network boundaries. Our security policy (legal/regulatory) states that transaction-level PII and payment details may not be processed by any third party outside our control. That rules out sending raw payloads to a Redwood-managed cluster, even if logs are disabled.

> 2) Do you require customer-managed KMS/HSM for model keying and log encryption, or is BYOK acceptable with Redwood-managed HSM?

Customer-managed KMS is a hard requirement for secrets and any encryption keys that protect sensitive payloads. We also prefer an HSM-backed key lifecycle if possible.

> 3) Are there any audit log retention/forwarding requirements (SIEM ingestion) that would force logs to remain on your network?

Yes audit logs must be forwarded to our Splunk instance within our VPC. Retention policy is 7 years for relevant events.

Given the above, we are leaning toward Private VPC or an on-prem package. That said, we're open to Private VPC where the control plane is managed by Redwood but all inference and logs remain in our VPC, with customer KMS and no egress.

Next step: Can Vivek and your team share a short checklist of network requirements and an initial list of ports/hosts so our infra team can validate? If Thursday works, we'll book the technical call.

Thanks,
Alex Morgan
Head of Platform Security | FinSecure Inc.
alex.morgan@finsecure.com | +1 212-555-0234

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation follow-up

Hi Alex 

Thanks for the detailed answers, super helpful. Quick technical notes and an initial checklist to help your infra team validate feasibility for a Private VPC deployment (control plane managed):

High-level options (summary):
- Private VPC (control plane managed by Redwood): Redwood control plane coordinates deployments, but inference workers run in a customer-managed VPC. No model payload egress. Support for customer-managed KMS (Cloud KMS/Azure Key Vault) and HSM-backed keys.
- On-prem (air-gapped): Full package we install/hand-off; required for customers with extreme isolation needs; includes optional offline model loading.

Initial network checklist (minimal):
- Outbound: Workers initiate outbound to Redwood control plane IPs on TCP 443 for heartbeat and orchestration. If your policy forbids any outbound, on-prem may be required.
- Ports: Allow egress to redwood-control.redwood-inference.com on 443; recommend whitelisting FQDN/IP range.
- KMS: TLS connectivity to your KMS endpoints (mutual TLS optional) list of endpoints we'll need.
- Logs: Fluentd/collector will forward audit events to your Splunk endpoint via egress from worker nodes. Alternatively we can push logs to an S3-compatible endpoint inside your VPC.
- Monitoring: Prometheus scraping optional can be kept internal to your VPC.

If the requirement is strictly "no outbound to any third-party endpoint," then on-prem will be the only path. If you can allow TLS egress to specific Redwood control-plane IPs for orchestration, Private VPC should satisfy your needs while giving our team the ability to manage runtime updates and SRE.

I've attached the Private VPC diagram Marissa included and will prepare a short one-page port/checklist for your infra team prior to the call.

Proposed times: Thu 2026-11-12 15:00 PST or Fri 2026-11-13 10:00 PST which works for you?

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
